whyTestArgs: Both packages, because the core's rules are pinned twice: by this crate's own tests of the core over the in-memory backend, and by the Windows driver's tests, which run a real core over a real ring, and a sabotage of the core that only the driver's tests catch would otherwise read as surviving. --no-fail-fast, so the doctests run even when the unit tests have already failed: the worked examples in win-durable-ioring's README.md are compiled as doctests and claim to break the build when a change invalidates them (DI-3.2.4); without this flag cargo stops at the first failing target, the doctests never run under any sabotage the unit tests catch, and nothing shows that claim is true.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: coverage ignores the provider's domains
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a write is covered only once every domain of its file has succeeded. A file both answer for would be covered by its flush alone, and a domain's success would cover writes in other domains.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a provider failure reaches every file
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a failure of domain D reaches the files whose domains contain D and the unknown ones. Reaching every file suspects writes in other domains, which is a wrong answer about what is at risk.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: an answer for an ended lineage is applied
sabotages.why: DI-D-42 and DI-D-44: an ended lineage is not live, and a late answer for it reports nothing. Applying it observes a failure for a lineage the instance no longer answers for.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a second answer for a domain is applied
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: each domain is answered once. A second answer would change a recorded outcome, and observe a failure after a success was already acted on.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a domain the provider does not serve is asked about
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the default answers for every domain the provider does not serve. Asking the provider about one makes the seal wait for an answer the provider owes nobody.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a request's domains are not sorted
sabotages.why: DI-D-44: a request names its domains in the order of their interned ids. The request test pushes a file declared out of order, so the order of first appearance differs.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: a request's domains are sorted stably
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. A seal's parts name each domain once, so a stable sort orders them as the unstable one does.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a seal records no domain it asked about
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the seal waits for every domain it asked about. Recording none lets it finish on its flushes, and refuses every answer as one it did not ask for.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a completion dropped unanswered answers nothing
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a completion dropped unanswered is a failure of its domain. Without it the seal stays pending forever and the consumer is never told, which guarantee 4 forbids.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a file with operations held for a gate is removed
sabotages.why: API.md section 8: a held operation is pushed to its file later, so removing the file strands it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: the lowest gate kept is the highest
sabotages.why: target_holds names the lowest gate in each lineage: the first a consumer must make durable (DI-D-103).

sabotages.name: CONTROL: an equal gate replaces the lowest
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. Two gates with the same id in one lineage are the same epoch, so which of them target_holds names changes no report: searched from the other end, the lowest is the same.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a failure does not hold its file
sabotages.why: API.md section 8: every write in an unresolved failure's suspect set holds its file, since healing it re-issues writes there.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a suspect write is also counted as uncovered
sabotages.why: IoTargetBusy.uncovered is outside every failure's suspect set; a suspect write is reported through its failure, and counting it twice tells the consumer to seal what sealing cannot clear.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a write in flight is also counted as uncovered
sabotages.why: A write in flight is the I/O core's to count; counting it here too reports it twice.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: the epoch to seal through is the lowest, not the highest
sabotages.why: IoTargetBusy.uncovered_through is what to seal through to clear every uncovered write; the lowest would clear only some.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: every failure is said to hold every file
sabotages.why: A failure holds a file only when its suspect set names a write to it; reporting the rest asks the consumer to resolve failures that do not concern the file.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a completion never clears its file's last operation
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: in_flight clears as completions arrive. A count left at one refuses the file forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: close hands back no held operation
sabotages.why: DI-D-25: close() returns the gated operations the kernel never saw, with their buffers and contexts; dropping them loses the consumer's buffers.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: close hands back no failure
sabotages.why: DI-D-25: close() returns the unresolved failures.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a completion is not counted when made
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: ending waits until the count is zero, so an uncounted completion is not waited for, and its answer is recorded as an inconsistency.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a heal is released by a seal that stops short of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: the releasing seal must reach the highest epoch pushed when the heal was made, or the mark passes the failed epoch while the re-issued writes are not committed.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a write in flight is not part of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: the re-issue is every write pushed before the heal. Without the pushed one, a seal short of it releases the heal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a held write is not part of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: a held write counts as pushed, so the releasing seal waits for it to be released and complete.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an unmatched import domain is not reported
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: a domain the instance was never given is reported, so a misspelling is not silent.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an inconsistency is not panicked on
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: an inconsistency is panicked on where it is found, in every build; carrying on would report from bookkeeping known to be wrong.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an inconsistency panics while unwinding
sabotages.why: DI-D-46 and the ring crate's D-79: a second panic while unwinding aborts the process and loses the first. The test binary aborts, which the harness counts as caught.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: an inconsistency is not reported to the sink
sabotages.why: DI-D-51 routes the inconsistency report through the consumer's sink; dropping it leaves a consumer who chose stderr, OutputDebugString or ETW with a panic and nothing in the place it watches.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: the core reports to a sink without asking whether it wants the event
sabotages.why: Asking first is what makes a sink that wants nothing cost a branch (DI-D-51 T2); not asking hands every event to every sink.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: a fan-out gives each event to every sink
sabotages.why: A fan-out hands an event that is not a pair's end only to the sinks that want its kind, so a sink's answer to wants means the same behind a fan-out as alone.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: a fan-out wants an event only when every sink does
sabotages.why: A fan-out wants what any of its sinks wants; requiring all of them would silence a stderr sink beside a deaf one.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full submission queue is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refusal names its cause. A backend that queues past its submission queue never tells the caller to submit.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full completion queue is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refusal names its cause. A backend that admits more than its completion queue holds never tells the caller to drain.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full submission queue is reported as needing a drain
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: the cause is what lets the caller act without probing; the wrong cause sends it to the wrong remedy.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a memory commit makes nothing durable
sabotages.why: A commit is what makes a memory target's bytes durable; without it a test cannot read what a commit warranted.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: the notification is raised on every submit that leaves completions
sabotages.why: DI-D-50 P10: the notification is raised on the transition from no completions to some, not on every submission.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a read past the end reports its whole buffer
sabotages.why: A read may complete short, and the count is the consumer's to handle; reporting the buffer's length claims bytes that were not read.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a buffer's address is not checked
sabotages.why: A target's geometry covers its buffers' addresses as well as its offsets and lengths; unbuffered I/O needs all three.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a submission for a detached target loses its buffer
sabotages.why: Buffers go in owned and come back (DI-D-50 P10), on a fault as on a success.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the memory backend tests emptiness by length
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the new code: an empty queue has length zero, so this is an equivalent change. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: needing both is not reported as needing a drain
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a caller told both must drain as well as submit; dropping the drain leaves it retrying into a full completion queue.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: an unknown refusal is called retryable
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: an unknown cause may never clear; calling it retryable invites a caller to loop on it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a length is checked against the offset's alignment
sabotages.why: A target's offsets and lengths may need different alignments; checking one against the other admits operations the target cannot take.
find: offset.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64) && length.is_multiple_of(self.length as u64)
replace: offset.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64) && length.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64)

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: zero is accepted as an alignment
sabotages.why: A Geometry always holds powers of two; zero would make every alignment check divide by zero.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a description drops the target's flush domains
sabotages.why: DI-D-50 P4: the core decides failure sharing from the domains a target declares; a description without them makes every target share fate with every other.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused write spends an operation id
sabotages.why: Only an accepted push spends an id, so accepted pushes' ids are consecutive; a refused one is undone whole (DI-D-52).

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused commit is dropped
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a commit the backend refuses is kept and emitted again; dropping it leaves its seal waiting forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused commit is not emitted with the next actions
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a kept commit rides on the next actions, so a driver that only acts on actions still issues it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: deliver is set whenever the queue holds entries
sabotages.why: Readiness is raised on the queue's transition from empty, as DI-D-28 sets the readiness event; raising it on every change wakes the consumer for nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a write is not recorded with the durability core
sabotages.why: A seal waits for, and commits, the writes recorded with it; one never recorded is neither waited for nor covered.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: an operation in flight is not counted against its target
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: removing a target is refused while operations on it are in flight.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a write's completion is not told to the durability core
sabotages.why: A seal commits only writes that completed; the core learns of completion here.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a failed operation is reported as a transfer
sabotages.why: A fault is reported on the operation's completion (the contract's obligations), never hidden as a zero-byte transfer.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: another core's lineage is taken for this one's
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: a lineage carries its instance, so another core's is refused rather than read as this one's of the same number.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a target with an operation in flight is removed
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: every hold refuses removal, operations in flight among them.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: an accepted operation is not recorded
sabotages.why: An accepted operation is in flight until its completion, which the core must recognise; one never recorded makes its own completion a breach.
find: self.issued(token, id, kind, target, context, false);

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the core's actions test emptiness by length
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the core: an empty vector has length zero, so this is an equivalent change. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a released operation is not recorded as issued
sabotages.why: DI-D-23: a held write is recorded in flight once its gate releases it; one never recorded is never waited for by a seal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a released operation the backend refuses is not kept
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: an operation the core emitted after its gate is the core's to keep and emit again, as a commit is.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an operation never issued is reported as transferred
sabotages.why: Guarantee 9: a held operation an abandoned epoch stopped ends as NeverIssued, naming the epoch, so the consumer knows nothing was written.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a gate on an abandoned epoch is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-43: an operation gated on an abandoned epoch could never be released, so it is refused at once.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a write closing a gate cycle is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-43: a write whose gate needs, transitively, the write itself would wait forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a gate in another core is taken for this one's
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: an epoch carries its lineage's instance, so a gate on another core's is refused rather than read as this core's of the same number.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an operation held for a gate does not hold its target
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: every hold refuses removal, operations held for a gate among them.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the default lineage can be ended
sabotages.why: The default lineage never ends while the core lives.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a busy lineage is reported retired
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: a lineage is retired only once nothing holds it, and a refusal says what does.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the core states a minted lineage's key type
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the lineage code: a lineage key is a u64, so naming the type changes nothing. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the core makes no requests of the provider
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a seal touching a served domain is answered by the provider; without its request the seal never finishes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: every provider answer is taken as success
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a provider's failure is a failure of its domain; taking it as success reports durable what was lost.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an answer for a domain the provider does not serve is accepted
sabotages.why: An answer the core never asked for is a protocol breach (DI-D-44); the core names it, rather than reading it as the seal's.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the durability core is not told what the provider serves
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the durability core asks the provider only for the domains it serves; without them a served target's seal waits for an answer never requested.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle accepts a short write
sabotages.why: DI-D-50: a write completes in full or with a fault; a short count is a target breaking its obligation.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle accepts a write longer than it asked
sabotages.why: A write transferring more than its length did not do what was pushed; in full means exactly.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle holds a read to its length
sabotages.why: A read may complete short (the contract); refusing one encodes a rule the contract does not make.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the core's tests do not report their seals to the oracle
sabotages.why: The oracle runs beside the core's tests (DI-D-24); a Durable for a seal it was never told of is DurableNotSealed, which only the oracle sees -- so this proves the binding is live.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a submission the backend refuses is dropped
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refused submission the core originated goes back to it, which keeps it and emits it again; dropped, its seal waits forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: the engine keeps no provider requests
sabotages.why: DI-D-44: the driver makes the provider's requests with its lock released, so the engine keeps them; dropped, a served seal never finishes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a drain stops after one pass
sabotages.why: The notification is an edge (the ring crate's D-19), so a drain runs until a pass pops nothing. A completion's act rings the doorbell itself, so one pass leaves something unissued only when that doorbell failed: the commit it pushed stays queued, and only the next pass issues it and pops what it completes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a drain reports no readiness
sabotages.why: DI-D-28: entries made poppable by a drain must be told, or a consumer waiting on readiness waits forever.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: act rings no doorbell
sabotages.why: A backend only queues what it is pushed, so the engine's act is what issues a batch. Without the doorbell nothing is issued until a completion drives a drain, and with none in flight, never.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a push rings the doorbell for itself as well as the batch
sabotages.why: The doorbell is rung once for a batch, which is what a ring is for: a push that rings its own makes one submission per push.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a failed doorbell is not told
sabotages.why: A doorbell that fails leaves what was pushed queued, with nothing in flight to drive a drain. Not told, the consumer waits for a completion that cannot come.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a refusal for want of room is not rung and tried once more
sabotages.why: A queue that is full is cleared by the doorbell, which the engine can ring at once; without the retry the push waits for a completion to re-emit it.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a consumer's push does not note its failed doorbell
sabotages.why: The driver tells the consumer, once, that a push is queued and its doorbell failed, so the consumer's pop rings it again and reports a cause that stays.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: the note of a failed doorbell is not cleared when taken
sabotages.why: Told once: a note that is not cleared tells the consumer on every push after.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a failed read of completions is forgotten
sabotages.why: The drain that could not read its completions ends, and the consumer's pop reports why; forgotten, the consumer is not told its ring cannot be read.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: the last fault is kept in place of the first
sabotages.why: The first fault is the one that explains the rest, and a second drain failing the same way must not replace it.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a drain that could not read goes on
sabotages.why: A backend that cannot read its completions ends the drain, and the consumer is told; going on reports nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a fault a later read got past is still reported
sabotages.why: A read that works after a failed one makes the fault stale, which the consumer is not told. Both clearing sites are removed together: either alone leaves the other clearing it, so each is equivalent by itself.

sabotages.name: PR-126: a write ending past isize::MAX is admitted
sabotages.why: A Vec holds at most isize::MAX bytes, so a write ending past it can only panic the target; check and push refuse it as malformed. Caught by the boundary test, one byte either side of the bound.

sabotages.name: PR-126: a target that cannot grow aborts instead of reporting it
sabotages.why: A write the target cannot find memory for completes with a fault and hands its buffer back, as every allocation that can fail is reported and not aborted on. Without the try_reserve the resize aborts the process, which the sweep sees as the suite dying: a weaker detection than an assertion, and the test that names the behaviour is the one that dies.

sabotages.name: PR-126: registered buffers are replaced while an operation is outstanding
sabotages.why: A queued or finished operation may name a registered region, which replacing the buffers invalidates; the builder refuses it as a caller's programming error. Caught by the two should_panic tests, one with an operation queued and one with a completion waiting.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the engine tests a pass's pops by comparison
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the engine: negating a bool and comparing it with false are the same test. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: an operation is held without asking the backend
sabotages.why: DI-D-54: a gated operation is put to the backend's check before it is held, so it is refused at push for what an ungated one would be. Unasked, a gated span on a backend with no registration is accepted, and fails only once released.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: every refusal of the core's own is kept
sabotages.why: DI-D-54: a submission refused for a cause that is not retryable can never be issued; kept, it is re-emitted forever and its operation never completes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: every refusal of the core's own ends it
sabotages.why: The other direction: a full queue clears once the driver submits or drains, so a submission refused for it is kept, not failed.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: a refusal fault does not carry its cause
sabotages.why: The REFUSED fault's error is the RefusalCause itself -- a static of it for a cause that carries nothing (DI-D-105) -- so a consumer recovers it by downcasting rather than parsing a message. Naming another cause's static reports the wrong one.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: a refusal fault drops the backend's code
sabotages.why: A cause carrying the backend's report keeps its code on the fault, as every fault the backend reports itself does.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: the engine does not act on what a refusal makes due
sabotages.why: A refusal that ends a submission makes its completion due -- a failure, an entry -- and the engine acts on it in the same call, so the readiness it raises is not lost.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: the memory backend's check admits everything
sabotages.why: check answers what push would refuse whatever the queues hold; one that admits everything lets the core hold what it can never issue.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the engine folds readiness by a longer spelling
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the reworked act: an equivalent spelling of the same fold must survive; caught would mean a test is matching incidental code.

sabotages.name: DI-7.1: a pool drain does not submit first
sabotages.why: Each pass of a drain begins by ringing the backend's doorbell, which issues what a failed doorbell left queued, so a consumer that has stopped popping still gets its work issued. Without it a drain runs and never asks the backend. Caught by the doorbell tests, which fail a doorbell and expect the next drain to issue what it left queued.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump drains before it waits
sabotages.why: The wait is for the completions the drain then takes. Drained first, a pump woken by a raising returns having taken nothing, and the entries are there only for the next one.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump waits holding the engine's lock
sabotages.why: The wait is for something another thread does, and doing it takes the lock: a push, a provider's answer, a handle's release. Held through the wait, nothing can wake the pump but its own timeout.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump whose wait failed does not drain
sabotages.why: A delivery that cannot wait still delivers what has completed, and says why it could not wait. Skipping the drain makes a broken notification stop an instance delivering at all.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump reports the drain's result inverted
sabotages.why: Whether entries became poppable is what sets the readiness event and what a consumer's loop keys on.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a delivery's shared slot is not its own
sabotages.why: A provider's answer and a handle's release reach the engine through the slot shared out; a slot of its own finds nothing there.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a construction's failure is not the backend's fault
sabotages.why: A construction that fails names why: the backend's own fault, as it reported it, since a fault is cloned without allocating (DI-D-105).

sabotages.name: DI-23.4.2: a fault made an io::Error loses its kind
sabotages.why: A fault converted to an io::Error keeps the kind of the io::Error its report holds, so a caller that matches on the kind still can, as it could when the pump's construction reported an io::Error.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification forgets what its wait saw
sabotages.why: A wait is for a raising since the last one that saw any. Forgetting makes every wait after the first return at once.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification's wait with no limit returns at once
sabotages.why: None is no limit: a wait that does not wait is a poll, and a pump with no limit would spin.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification's timeout is ignored
sabotages.why: A wait that returns before its timeout reports no raising when one was about to come.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification reports a raising when it timed out
sabotages.why: Whether it was raised is the answer the wait exists to give; the boundary is a count equal to the one already seen.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: DI-7.3: a pump asks whether the drain made entries poppable another way
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the new module: map_or(false, ..) is is_some_and(..), so this must survive; if it comes back caught, something is matching incidental text.

sabotages.name: DI-7.5: a pump does not drain before it waits
sabotages.why: The notification is an edge: the completions that raised it may have been taken by another waiter on the same event, and waiting for a raising that has happened blocks while they sit in the backend.

sabotages.name: DI-7.5: a pump whose first drain delivered reports none
sabotages.why: A first drain that delivered returns that it did, which sets the readiness event and tells the consumer to pop.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: a write-only access is said to be able to read
sabotages.why: Whether an access can read is what the backends ask, so a write-only access that said it could read would let a read through to a target that cannot serve it.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: the read-only marker names the read and write access
sabotages.why: A target made from a read-only handle states what the marker names, so a marker that named another access would state more than the handle was opened with.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: a description states a different access than its target
sabotages.why: What the core decides with is the description, taken once, so a description that did not carry the target's access would leave the refusal to a backend that has already been told otherwise.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: a refusal for access ends an operation with some other cause
sabotages.why: The fault a refused operation of the core's own ends with carries the cause, and a refusal for access is AccessDenied, not another cause the downcast would find.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: the in-memory backend lets a write through to a target that cannot write
sabotages.why: A write is covered by a target that can write.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: the in-memory backend lets a read through from a target that cannot read
sabotages.why: A read is covered by a target that can read.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: the in-memory backend refuses a commit to a target that cannot write
sabotages.why: A commit is not covered or refused by access: it is issued only to a target with writes, and a target that cannot write has none, so no rule is made for it.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9: the in-memory backend does not refuse what the access does not cover
sabotages.why: An operation the access does not cover is refused as AccessDenied.

sabotages.name: DI-13.9 control: a target states its access through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same value returned through a local, which no test can tell apart.

sabotages.name: DI-13.10: a key declaring more than its target states is admitted
sabotages.why: Registration refuses a key whose declaration the target does not cover. Admitting exactly those it does cover, and refusing the rest, is the one runtime step a typed key adds.

sabotages.name: DI-13.10: a typed key declares some other access than its marker names
sabotages.why: What a key declares is what its marker says; a key that always declared read and write would be admitted by every target that can do both and refused by none it should be.

sabotages.name: DI-13.10: an untyped key declares an access
sabotages.why: An untyped key declares nothing, so any target registers under it and the core judges what is pushed.

sabotages.name: DI-13.10: an access covers what it cannot do
sabotages.why: An access covers another when it can do everything the other can, so joining the two axes with an or covers a key that declares one axis the target lacks.

sabotages.name: DI-13.10 control: a typed key's number is taken through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same number returned through a local, which no test can tell apart.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a failed write is applied to the target anyway
sabotages.why: Fail must leave the target as it was; applying it and then reporting the fault is FailAfterApplying, which is a different and separately tested fault.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a write failed after applying is reported as having succeeded
sabotages.why: The fault is the point of the variant: a write whose bytes are in the target and which is reported failed.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a short count is ignored
sabotages.why: A short write is what the fault exists to produce; ignoring the count completes it in full.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a short count larger than the buffer transfers the count
sabotages.why: The transfer is at most the count and never more than the buffer holds; max would slice past the end and panic.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a held completion is delivered at once
sabotages.why: Holding is withholding the completion until the test releases it; delivering it at once is an ordinary completion.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a late completion of zero doorbells is held
sabotages.why: Zero is an ordinary completion; held with a count of zero it would be aged below zero by the next doorbell.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a late completion is aged by two doorbells at a time
sabotages.why: A completion late by two doorbells is released after two, and not after one.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a held completion takes no room in the completion queue
sabotages.why: A held completion is outstanding: if it took no room, a completion might have nowhere to go when it is released.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: the notification is raised when the completions were not empty
sabotages.why: The notification is raised on a transition from none to some; raising it on every release or doorbell into a non-empty queue wakes a waiter for nothing, and not raising it into an empty one loses the wakeup.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a scripted refusal is never consulted at the push
sabotages.why: The refusal is applied at the push; consulted at the wrong point it never fires.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a step counts only when no earlier step has fired
sabotages.why: Every matching step counts every occurrence, so a step's count does not depend on the steps before it.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: from fires one occurrence late
sabotages.why: From n is the nth match and every one after it.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: nth fires on every match from the nth
sabotages.why: Nth is that match and no other.

sabotages.name: DI-11.1: a step ignores the target it names
sabotages.why: A step that names a target fires only for operations on it.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.4: a lock wait's end is written before the lock is taken

sabotages.name: DI-12.1.3: the line prefix drops its space
sabotages.why: The prefix is what a reader of a line, and every sink that writes one, relies on being the same: `dioring:`, a space, and the event.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.1: a domain claimed twice is not refused
sabotages.why: A domain routed to two providers is refused at build (DI-2.12 point 1): with no refusal the router would serve it twice and the core would refuse the whole instance with less to go on.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.1: the refusal names the second registration twice
sabotages.why: The refusal names both registrations, so a consumer can find the two that claim the domain; naming one twice reads as a provider that declared it twice.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.1: the union is read in reverse registration order
sabotages.why: The router's domains are the registrations in order, each in its own order, which is what a consumer reading them back, and the core interning them, see.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.1 control: the routes are gathered without a capacity
sabotages.why: A control: the same routes gathered without reserving room first, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.2: every part goes to the first registration
sabotages.why: Each domain's part goes to the provider that serves it (DI-D-81); a part given to another provider is flushed by something that never said it could.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.2: a provider with no part is called anyway
sabotages.why: One call per provider that has parts: a provider called with an empty request is asked for work it was never given, and a provider that rejects that would fail a seal it had no part in.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.2: an unrouted domain is sent to the first registration instead of panicked on
sabotages.why: A domain no provider serves is a caller breaking the protocol and is panicked on where it is found (DI-D-46, DI-D-83); sending it to a provider hands work to something that never said it could do it, and lets the breach persist.

sabotages.name: DI-12.2.2 control: the per-provider parts are made by counting
sabotages.why: A control: the same empty parts made by counting the routes instead of walking them, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.1: an id is minted whether or not the sink wants the pair
sabotages.why: An id is minted only for a pair a sink wants (DI-D-80), so a sink that wants nothing costs the counter nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.1: the counter is not advanced
sabotages.why: Every id differs from every other the process minted, which a counter that does not move breaks at the second mint.

sabotages.name: DI-19.1: the counter starts at zero
sabotages.why: The first id is 1, as the documentation says.

sabotages.name: DI-19.1 control: the counter is advanced with sequential consistency
sabotages.why: A control: a stronger ordering than relaxed, which mints the same distinct ids and no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1: an end of another kind than its begin is accepted
sabotages.why: A pair's begin and end are one kind, so a sink wants both or neither (DI-D-87); an end of another kind is a different pair's, or a defect.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1: an end that does not repeat its begin's identity is accepted
sabotages.why: An end repeats its begin's identity fields (DI-D-87), so a reader of one line knows what ended; the checker is where that is held.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1: an ended pair is forgotten
sabotages.why: Nothing of a pair follows its end; a checker that forgets the end lets a second end, or a begin again, pass as something else.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1: a pair named as left open need not be open
sabotages.why: The finish is bidirectional: every open pair is named, and every named pair is open, so a test cannot excuse a pair that never began.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1: a lock wait's end is taken for a begin
sabotages.why: Which events open and close a pair is defined once, by Diagnostic::pairing (DI-D-87), which the checker and the ETW sink both read.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.1 control: the open pairs are gathered by cloning
sabotages.why: A control: the same ids gathered by clone instead of copy, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2: a seal answered durable leaves its pair open
sabotages.why: A seal's pair ends at its first answer (DI-D-87); one left open is a begin with no end, which the pairing checker refuses.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2: a seal answered blocked leaves its pair open
sabotages.why: Blocked is an answer, so it ends the seal's pair; left open, the pair would end later as durable, saying the wrong answer.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2: a seal whose flush failed ends as durable
sabotages.why: A failure of a seal's own flush is its answer, and its pair ends saying so.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2: a lineage that ends leaves its pairs open
sabotages.why: An end is reported on every path a begin can leave by (DI-D-87); a lineage that ends answers nothing more, so its pairs end with it.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2: the core dropped leaves its pairs open
sabotages.why: An instance closed or dropped answers nothing more, so every pair still open ends as it does.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.2 control: the abandoned flushes are ordered by a stable sort
sabotages.why: A control: the same order by a stable sort, which no test can tell apart since the keys are distinct. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.3: a lock wait's begin is not reported
sabotages.why: A wait is a pair whose begin is written when the immediate try fails (DI-D-87); an end with no begin is what the pairing checker refuses.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.3: a lock wait's end is not reported
sabotages.why: The end is written as the lock is taken, with it held (DI-D-80); a wait whose end never comes is a pair left open.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.3 control: the taken guard is declared with its type spelled
sabotages.why: A control: the same binding with its type written out, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.4: a provider's abandoned domain ends as failed
sabotages.why: A flush's end says how it ended (DI-D-87): a domain its provider abandoned did not fail, and an end that says it did sends a reader after a failure that did not happen.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.4: a provider's failed domain ends as succeeded
sabotages.why: A failed domain whose end says it succeeded hides the failure the pair exists to show.

sabotages.name: DI-19.2.5: the one definition calls a seal's end a begin
sabotages.why: DI-19.2.5: Diagnostic::pairing is the one definition of which events pair (DI-D-88). Changing it must fail this suite through the code that binds to it; a suite that held a copy of the rule would pass.

sabotages.name: DI-22.1: a pair's end is asked of wants
sabotages.why: A sink that stopped wanting a kind while a pair was open is not given the end, so a sink that holds something for the pair from its begin never lets it go: the ETW sink's activity map grew by a pair for each session stop. DI-D-96.

sabotages.name: DI-22.1: a begin is taken for an end
sabotages.why: The edge decides which events skip the question. Reading a begin as an end gives every sink every begin, wanted or not, and asks the end.

sabotages.name: DI-22.1 control: the end is read by another spelling
sabotages.why: A control: `map_or(false, ..)` is `is_some_and(..)`, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-23.1: popping an entry allocates
sabotages.why: The allocation test (tests/allocation.rs) pins how many allocations each phase of the core makes, so an allocation added to a path is seen. Without it the measurement DI-M23 lowers would not notice a new one. DI-D-97.

sabotages.name: DI-23.2: a tagged call sets no tag
sabotages.why: Every allocation the core makes runs under a tag the allocation test reads (DI-D-104). If tagging sets nothing, every counted allocation is untagged, and the test's rule that none is must report it, phase by phase.

sabotages.name: DI-23.2: two calls share one tag
sabotages.why: A tag names one allocating call (DI-D-104). The guard records where each was made, so the allocation test must report a tag seen from two places in the source, naming both.

sabotages.name: DI-23.2 control: a tag no scenario reaches is renamed
sabotages.why: A control, and a limit stated: the allocation test pins only the tags its scenarios reach. A gate cycle the search found and the trace did not is never reached, so its tag's name is seen by nothing. The rules hold for the paths exercised; the static pass is what covers the rest.

sabotages.name: DI-23.4.2: a refusal carrying a fault reports the backend's report and not its cause
sabotages.why: Unusable and Unknown carry the backend's fault, so their cause is shared rather than static (DI-D-105); the backend's own report is only the fallback when that allocation fails. Reporting it always loses the downcast to RefusalCause that DI-D-54 promises.

sabotages.name: DI-23.4.2: a shared report ignores the allocator it was given
sabotages.why: The seam a test reaches the fallback through is the allocator; sharing from the global one regardless never reaches the fallback a failed allocation must take.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a write named to a seal stays in the unsealed span
sabotages.why: Naming a write moves it from its lineage's unsealed span to the seal's. Leaving it charged to the unsealed entry too counts it twice, so that entry outlives its last write; the core's census of the uncovered writes sees an entry no write is in.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a span entry is never released
sabotages.why: An entry is released with its last write, or entries outgrow the uncovered writes and the window no longer bounds them (DI-D-107). The census sees an entry with no write.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a seal flushes a file once per write
sabotages.why: A seal's flush of a file is charged once, to the file's entry in the seal's span; issuing it for every write named issues the same flush again for each.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a file's flush may be answered twice
sabotages.why: Each issued flush answers once; a second answer for the same file is the driver or the kernel breaking its contract (DI-D-46), and must be refused as inconsistent rather than counted again.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a write is covered whether or not its file's flush succeeded
sabotages.why: Coverage needs the flush of the write's own file, in its seal's span, to have succeeded. Accepting any entry covers a file whose flush failed when another file of the same seal succeeds.

sabotages.name: DI-23.6: a lost write is reported by the first rather than the last
sabotages.why: The control. Which lost write the inconsistency names, when several are lost in one let-go, changes no state and no outcome; a test failing here would be asserting the message's choice of example.

sabotages.why: What trailed a recorded seal is next in order once the mark passes it; dropping it loses a seal the consumer made, which is never answered.

sabotages.name: DI-23.7: an empty seal behind a failure is not answered
sabotages.why: An empty seal finished but held by a failure is answered Blocked, as a recorded one is; leaving it unanswered leaves the consumer no answer to its seal.

sabotages.name: DI-23.7: an empty seal releases no heal
sabotages.why: A heal is released by the first seal made after it that reaches the re-issue (DI-D-41, DI-D-46), empty or not; an empty seal releasing nothing leaves the heal held until a recorded seal comes.

sabotages.name: DI-23.7: an empty seal takes no sequence number
sabotages.why: A heal is released by a seal made after it, known by its sequence number; an empty seal that took none would share the next seal's, so one made before a heal would release it.

sabotages.name: DI-23.7: finishing empty seals looks past a seal not started
sabotages.why: The control. A seal not started has a write at or below it outstanding, so no empty seal after it is ready either; the break only stops looking. Continuing changes nothing a test could see.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a recorded write holds no place
sabotages.why: A write holds its place while uncovered (DI-D-107). Without the hold the uncovered writes outgrow the places counted, so a consumer that never seals is never refused; the census sees a write with no place.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a failure holds none of the places of the writes it suspects
sabotages.why: A failure holds the places of its suspect writes until resolved (DI-D-100), after the writes are covered or failed. Without it a failure outlives the places that bound its suspect set.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: an abandoned failure keeps its places
sabotages.why: Resolving a failure lets go of the places it held; one that never does leaves them counted for ever and shrinks the window for good.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a healed failure keeps its places
sabotages.why: A heal that takes effect resolves its failure as an abandon does; its places must go with it.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a write that is no longer uncovered keeps its place
sabotages.why: A write covered, failed or let go with its lineage stops holding its place as an uncovered write; one that does not leaves the places counted past the writes.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: popping an operation's completion lets go of nothing
sabotages.why: An operation holds its place until its completion is popped; popping must let it go, or a consumer that pops everything still fills the window.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a held operation takes no place
sabotages.why: An operation held for its gate spends an operation id and holds its place from then (DI-D-107); one that takes none lets a consumer hold any number.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a pushed operation takes no place
sabotages.why: An operation the backend took holds its place from its push; one that takes none, a read most of all since nothing else holds a read, is uncounted.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: two failures hold a place once between them
sabotages.why: Each unresolved failure suspecting a write holds its place, so the place stays until every one is resolved; counting them as one frees the place when the first is.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: a place with only a failure holding it is let go
sabotages.why: A place ends only when no holder is left. A failure's hold alone must keep it: that is how a covered, failed or popped write stays counted while it is suspected.

sabotages.name: DI-23.8.1: an operation admitted twice is not reported
sabotages.why: Admitting an operation twice is the core's own bookkeeping gone wrong (DI-D-46) and must be reported, not absorbed into one place.

sabotages.name: DI-23.9: a later Durable does not remove the older
sabotages.why: A lineage has at most one un-popped Durable (DI-D-101); without the removal a consumer that pops slowly finds one per seal, and the queue grows with the seals a consumer makes.

sabotages.name: DI-23.9: the later Durable is written over the older in place

sabotages.name: DI-23.9: a Durable replaces the un-popped Durable of any lineage

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage lets go a write whose flush is out
sabotages.why: A write named to a seal whose commit is out keeps its place and its entry until the commit answers (DI-D-98); letting it go at the end leaves a commit in flight that nothing in the window accounts for.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage keeps a write whose flush has answered
sabotages.why: Only a flush still out keeps a write: one that has answered is the lineage's no longer, and keeping its write holds a place no answer will release.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage keeps a write whose flush was never issued
sabotages.why: A file only the provider answers for has no commit out; keeping its write holds a place no flush will release.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage lets go the writes of every lineage
sabotages.why: Ending a lineage lets go its own writes and no other's.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage lets go a write still in flight
sabotages.why: A write in flight is let go as it completes, so that a failure observed meanwhile can still mark it.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage keeps every seal
sabotages.why: What an ended lineage keeps of its seals is those with a flush out, to find the writes the flush lets go; keeping the rest keeps the lineage unretired for ever.

sabotages.why: Seal numbers count a lineage's own seals, so two lineages' seals share one; the answer for an ended lineage lets go that lineage's writes alone.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: a flush of an ended lineage lets go the writes of every file
sabotages.why: Each file has a flush of its own, and the writes of the others stay until theirs answers.

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: a flush of an ended lineage lets go the writes of every seal

sabotages.name: DI-23.5.2.1: an ended lineage is retired with a flush still out
